name: 程聖倫
objective: The objective of this course is to prepare students to understand the current theories, practices, tools and techniques in knowledge management (KM) to deal with the challenges with the organization and management of knowledge. This course addresses contemporary issues in managing knowledge, intellectual capital and other intangible assets by discussing the fundamental concepts of knowledge and its creation, acquisition, representation, dissemination, use and re-use, the role and use of knowledge in organizations and institutions, KM systems and its application in knowledge generation and transfer, and in the representation, organization, and exchange of knowledge, knowledge codification and system development, its testing, KM tools and portals, and finally ethical, managerial and legal issues in knowledge management.
schedule:
Topics:

FOUNDATION (Weeks 1-2)
Week 1: Course Introduction & Introduction to Knowledge Management

*Overview of KM as a discipline
*Introduction to the Dalkir Meta-KM Process framework

Week 2: Knowledge Management Models & The KM Cycle

*Theoretical frameworks
*Understanding the create-share-use cycle
*R Lab intro: Setting up R environment, basic text data handling

PHASE 1: CREATE OR CAPTURE (Weeks 3-5)
Week 3: Knowledge Capture and Codification (Theory)

*Tacit vs. explicit knowledge
*Documentation strategies
*Knowledge elicitation techniques

Week 4: Knowledge Capture (R Lab I)

*R Lab: Text mining basics - extracting knowledge from documents
*Word frequencies, tf-idf, document similarity (tm, tidytext)

Week 5: Knowledge Discovery & Topic Modeling

*R Lab: Topic modeling with LDA - discovering knowledge domains
*Identifying hidden themes in organizational documents (topicmodels, stm)

PHASE 2: SHARE AND DISSEMINATE (Weeks 6-8)
Week 6: Organizational Culture, Motivation, and Knowledge Sharing

*Organizational culture as enabler/barrier to knowledge sharing
*Motivational factors (goal orientations) in knowledge contribution and knowledge hoarding 
*Achievement goal theory applied to KM behaviors
*Reward systems and cultural dimensions

Week 7: Measuring Culture, Motivation & Sharing Behaviors

*R Lab: Survey analysis & psychometrics
*Measuring organizational culture for KM
*Knowledge sharing attitudes and motivation scales
*Reliability analysis, CFA validation (lavaan, psych)

Week 8: Knowledge Sharing Networks & Communities of Practice

*Social capital and network perspectives
*Communities of practice frameworks
*R Lab: Social Network Analysis I & II
*Mapping knowledge sharing behaviors
*Network density, centrality, community detection (igraph, tidygraph, ggraph)

MID-TERM (Week 9)
Week 9: Mid-term Presentation

*ASSESS: Knowledge Mining & Discovery (Weeks 10-12)

Week 10: Knowledge Mining I - Pattern Discovery

*Association rules in organizational knowledge
*Finding expertise patterns*
*R Lab: Association rules mining (arules, arulesViz)

Week 11: Knowledge Mining II - Expertise Mapping

*Identifying subject matter experts
*Knowledge flow analysis
*R Lab: Combining text mining + SNA for expertise identification

Week 12: Sentiment Analysis & Knowledge Communication

*Analyzing organizational communication patterns
*Understanding knowledge sharing tone and effectiveness
*R Lab: Sentiment analysis of emails, documents, collaboration tools (tidytext, syuzhet)

PHASE 3: USE, APPLY AND RE-USE (Weeks 13-14)
Week 13: Knowledge Application & Organizational Learning

*Knowledge reuse strategies
*Learning from experience
*Lessons learned systems
*R Lab: Document clustering - organizing knowledge for reuse (K-means, hierarchical)

Week 14: Organizational Memory & Knowledge Retention

*Memory systems and repositories
*Knowledge loss prevention
*R Lab: Time-based analysis - tracking knowledge evolution and retention patterns

Week 15: Knowledge Management Strategy & Measurement

*KM strategy alignment with business goals
*Measuring KM value and ROI
*KM metrics and dashboards
*R Lab: Integration project - combining multiple analytical methods

CONTEXTUALIZE: Technology & Implementation (Week 16)
Week 16: KM Tools, Technology Infrastructure & The KM Team

*ICT infrastructure for KM
*KM governance and team roles
*Implementation challenges and change management
*R Lab: Building KM dashboards and final project support

LOOKING FORWARD & FINAL (Weeks 17-18)
Week 17: Future Challenges for KM & Emerging Trends

*AI and machine learning in KM
*Remote work and distributed knowledge

Week 18: Final
